subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: copying AI output as homework [Pitfall]
passage: On Sunday night, with three questions left and her eyes drooping, Damini pasted the science question into an AI tool, copied its neat paragraph about the water cycle into her notebook and went to bed. On Monday she handed in the homework and felt clever. On Wednesday Yusuf Sir asked her to explain, in her own words, why water vapour condenses higher up. Damini's mouth opened; nothing came. She could remember the shape of the paragraph, not its meaning. The class waited in silence. On Friday the test had a similar question with different numbers, and she stared at the page. She wrote two half-sentences and put her pen down. She got 4 out of 10. It wasn't that she couldn't learn it; the learning simply never happened.

qa.q: What did Damini do on Sunday night?
qa.a: Damini pasted the science question into an AI tool and copied its neat paragraph into her notebook.

qa.q: How did Damini feel on Wednesday when asked to explain?
qa.a: Damini felt embarrassed and stuck, since her mouth opened and nothing came.

qa.q: What could Damini try next time?
qa.a: Damini could ask the tool to explain the idea, then write her own answer, or ask Yusuf Sir for help, since explaining in her own words makes the learning happen.

qa.q: How might Yusuf Sir see that moment in class?
qa.a: Yusuf Sir probably becomes concerned and realises she has not really learned it, since she cannot explain what her homework says.

grounding: A teen pastes an AI-written answer as homework, then cannot explain it in class or solve a similar problem on the test, since the learning never happened.
